name: Gradient Boosting Classification Benchmark
description: This work explores the use of gradient boosting in the context of classification. Four popular implementations, including original GBM algorithm and selected state-of-the-art gradient boosting frameworks (i.e. XGBoost, LightGBM and CatBoost), have been thoroughly compared on several publicly available real-world datasets of sufficient diversity. In the study, special emphasis was placed on hyperparameter optimization, specifically comparing two tuning strategies, i.e. randomized search and Bayesian optimization using the Tree-stuctured Parzen Estimator. The performance of considered methods was investigated in terms of common classification accuracy metrics as well as runtime and tuning time. Additionally, obtained results have been validated using appropriate statistical testing. An attempt was made to indicate a gradient boosting variant showing the right balance between effectiveness, reliability and ease of use.
evaluation_method: accuracy (primary), with runtime and hyperparameter tuning time reported
reputation: A practical comparative study of gradient boosting implementations used by practitioners; valued for implementation-level insights rather than as a canonical benchmark.
notes: Focuses on tabular datasets and compares implementations (GBM, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost); results are dataset- and tuning-dependent. Includes runtime/tuning trade-offs; not an LLM benchmark.
